Subject: On-prem VPC deployment — control plane & data plane review

Hi Anita,

Thanks again for walking through Acme Cloud's requirements earlier. Attached are the initial reference diagrams and a checklist for the on-prem VPC deployment we discussed. High-level notes:

- Control plane: optional hosted control plane (customer-managed VPC peering) vs private control plane inside your VPC. We recommend private control plane inside a dedicated management subnet for regulated workloads.
- Data plane: colocated inference clusters inside your tenant VPC (dedicated subnets, strict SGs), with NAT gateway for outbound model pulls only.
- Networking: strict egress whitelisting, optional transit gateway for multi-region connectivity, and an ingress load balancer with mTLS.

Action items before our architecture call:
1) Review the attached 'redwood-vpc-diagram-v1.pdf' and flag any CIDR conflicts.
2) Confirm whether Acme requires the control plane to be fully customer-managed or if a lightweight managed-control option is acceptable.
3) Share any on-prem NOC firewall policies that could affect KV cache replication.

I'll loop in Vivek for kernel/runtime-level constraints we should avoid. Proposed call: Tue 16 Jun, 10:00 - 10:30 PT. Does that work?

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

- Preferred control plane model: Acme prefers the control plane to be customer-managed inside our VPC due to compliance. We can evaluate a read-only managed-control option later, but initial deployments must be fully under our control.
- CIDR: We have a 10.20.0.0/16 space reserved; could you confirm suggested subnets so we can check overlap with our on-prem ranges?
- Firewall constraints: Our on-prem firewalls block outbound on non-standard ports; we will need a short list of ports/IPs for model pulls and KV replication.

We can do Tue 16 Jun at 10:00 PT — I'll have our sysops join.

Subject: Re: On-prem VPC deployment — control plane & data plane review

Anita, Karthik — thanks. A couple of engineering clarifications and a proposed reference topology below. Attaching an SVG dataflow diagram (vpc-controlplane-dataflow.svg) with component-level flows. Key points:

1) Control plane (customer-managed inside VPC):
   - Deploy a small, HA control plane (2 nodes) inside a management subnet (e.g., 10.20.254.0/26). Management subnet must allow outbound TLS to Redwood's model registry endpoints (we can give explicit FQDNs/IP ranges).
   - Control plane communicates with Redwood telemetry endpoints only over TLS; no inbound access required from Redwood to the control plane.

2) Data plane (inference clusters):
   - Worker subnets: allocate 10.20.10.0/22 and 10.20.14.0/22 for inference nodes.
   - KV cache replication: uses gRPC over port 9701 (configurable). If your NOC blocks non-standard ports, we can tunnel replication over TLS (443) or use an egress-only proxy.

3) Networking & Security:
   - NAT gateway for model pulls/outbound only, restrict to FQDN/IP allowlist.
   - mTLS between client-facing LB and inference frontends; recommend a private CA or your KMS for certs.
   - No public IPs on worker nodes; health checks from ELB should be done via internal target groups.

4) Operational constraints:
   - Kernel-level optimizations: avoid transparent hugepages and ensure low-latency IRQ balancing; we'll provide a runtime tuning guide (see network-checklist.xlsx).
   - Disk: local NVMe recommended for KV cache, with periodic snapshots to your object storage endpoint.

Actionable asks from Acme before the call:
A) Confirm whether NOC can open port 9701, or if we should plan for TLS tunneling on 443.
B) Approve the suggested management subnet (10.20.254.0/26) or propose an alternative.
C) Share your internal CA or KMS process for cert issuance.

Happy to walk through the SVG diagram on the call and mark changes live.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Thanks Vivek — this is helpful. Quick answers ahead of the call:

- Port 9701: our NOC will not open non-standard ports by default. Please prepare the tunnel option (replication over 443) as Plan B.
- Management subnet: 10.20.254.0/26 is acceptable. We'll reserve it.
- Certs: we use HashiCorp Vault for cert issuance; I will share the process doc during the call.

We'll join the Tue 16 Jun 10:00 PT slot — sysops and one of our networking engineers (Raj) will be on the call. I attached a trimmed firewall sample for your infra team to review.

-Anita
